verses.verse:
हृत्कम्पःकण्ठः कम्पश्च जिह्वा मूलस्य कम्पनम्।
तथैवाधर कम्पश्च कराग्रौ कम्पितौ क्वचित्।७०।
verses.text: Vibration of the heart, vibration of the throat, vibration of the root of the tongue, and likewise vibration of the adhara (lips); and sometimes the fingertips are made to vibrate.

commentary.text: That is, the vibration that comes from an exercise like the way a dog keeps panting in the hot season is called hṛtkampa, that is, heart vibration. For the bānsurī this is the best vibration. Some people make the vibration with the throat — that is middling. And some people make the lips or the hands vibrate — this is the lowest. The practitioner should practise the best kind of breath close to a guru (teacher), for otherwise one does not see one's own faults. To blow into the Tripurā bānsurī, one should close the open end of the bamboo from three sides and blow slantwise from one side; it is mainly because the breath is connected with three sides that it is named Tripurā. This is what the following śloka says.

subsection.title: Practice of the Tongue and of the Fingers
